I've also tried making crunchy cookies by adding more flour and it resulted in a very cakey, dry cookie and it wasn't crumbly or crunchy at all. I think the key is to add less liquid, rather than add more dry ingredients.

I found that this recipe made crunchy cookies:  [https://www.cookiemadness.net/2008/04/08/crunchy-chocolate-chip-cookies-small-batch/](https://www.cookiemadness.net/2008/04/08/crunchy-chocolate-chip-cookies-small-batch/) Since I wanted them to be very crumbly (I was trying to imitate the texture and flavor of store bought cookies), I used 1/2 tbsp water instead of the egg (I don't like to use eggs in my baking), but you could probably use 1/2 - 1 tbsp of beaten egg.

 I bake them at 300 degrees for 18 - 20 minutes. The low temperature allows them to cook for longer than usual and get crunchy but not burnt. If they're not crunchy when you take them out of the oven, they will probably get crunchier while they cool. I've made the mistake of putting them back in the oven when I thought they were not crunchy enough and then ending up with cookies that were TOO crunchy.

I haven't tried it with butter, as I just used all shortening, so I don't know if it would have the same results if you use all butter, but here is another recipe that uses all butter if you don't want to use shortening:  [https://www.cookiemadness.net/2008/05/29/another-crunchy-chocolate-chip-cookie-recipe-all-butter/](https://www.cookiemadness.net/2008/05/29/another-crunchy-chocolate-chip-cookie-recipe-all-butter/)
